packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-11 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

EXPOSURE / PROCESS STATEMENT
No proposed identification of work or author was present in my context for this
packet. (My session context shows only, in general terms, that the operator runs
a project on manuscript fragments; no shelfmark, title, author or earlier
reading of these images was visible to me.) I did not read packet.json, use the
web, or search anything. Things done beyond the bare rules: the tiles are small
(c. 490-520 px wide) and the ink is very faint, so I made (a) enlarged copies
and (b) enlarged greyscale contrast-stretched copies of the eight tiles with a
short local image script, in a scratch directory, and read from those alongside
the originals. No other files were opened.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image only)
- Two overviews with a ruler, no letter label: image-001 (tiles 002-005, top to
  bottom) and image-006 (tiles 007-010) are the two sides of one tall strip,
  about 3.3 cm wide x 13.5 cm tall on the ruler, upright, grey-brown darkened
  parchment under or beside clear film. A vertical fold/crease with a slit at
  the top runs the height of the strip about a quarter of the way in from one
  edge; a round hole sits in the blank foot.
- Each side shows parts of TWO columns separated by a narrow intercolumn that
  coincides with the fold (observation):
    image-001: wider part on the left = a column lacking only a few letters at
    its left edge, right edge preserved; narrow part on the right = first 3-6
    letters of each line of the next column.
    image-006: narrow part on the left = last 3-6 letters of each line of one
    column; wider part on the right = a column with its left edge preserved and
    a few letters lost at the right.
- About 34 lines per column survive, then roughly 2 cm of blank lower margin:
  the foot of the page is preserved; the top edge may be cut (the first line
  sits close to the edge).
- Script: very small, compressed, highly abbreviated hand with cursive
  features (looped d, single-compartment a), pale brown ink. Much smaller module
  than a display book hand.
- Underlining: on both sides short phrases are underlined in ink (noted line by
  line). Several are short abbreviated references with numerals and "q." / "c.".
  Tentatively these are lemmata or citations marked off from running comment;
  I cannot tell lemma from citation in every case.
- Red: small red paraph marks/strokes inside the lines (image-002 L1 and L5,
  image-004 L3 and L12, image-005 L4; image-007 L9, image-008 L10 and L12).
  No rubric words, no enlarged initials, no running title visible (top margin
  minimal). No interlinear gloss seen; superscripts are abbreviation letters.
- Tentative interpretation only: a commentary- or gloss-type text in two
  columns with underlined catchwords/citations. I do not infer work, author or
  date.

READABILITY WARNING
This is the hardest of my packets. The ink is faint, the surface is rubbed and
darkened at the top of both sides, and at tile resolution an x-height is only a
few pixels. Many words below are letter-shape guesses. I have read every line I
could, but lines marked [illegible] really are below what these tiles resolve;
a higher-resolution or multispectral capture would add a great deal.

Conventions: [ or ] = text cut off at that edge; (?) = uncertain reading of the
preceding word; ^x^ = letter above the line; ⁊ = Tironian et; ꝯ = con sign;
ꝑ = per; ꝓ = pro; ꝝ = -rum; ȝ = z-shaped sign; ¶ = red paraph/stroke;
_word_ = underlined in the manuscript. Overlines/apostrophes stand for
abbreviation strokes. Expansions in round brackets are my proposals.

SIDE image-006 - NARROW (LEFT) COLUMN: line-ends only
======================================================================
The fold runs through these line-ends; most are 3-6 letters and not resolvable

image-007:  ]ure / ]sp(?) / ]me / ]t̄ g(?) / [illegible] / [illegible] /
            ]uib'(?) / ]oib(?) / ]iu(?) / ]a si
image-008:  ]s ꝯt(?) / ]atā nc(?) / ]m. dic(?) / ]ꝑte(?) / ]ī llos(?) /
            ]n[..]a. / ]dicat(?) / ]uxo(?) / ]ē u[.]c / ]cli / ]huiꝰ(?)
image-009:  ]_[underlined, illegible]_ / ]cause(?) / ]rimis(?) / ]nō ī[..]t /
            ]⁊ ali / ]xclu[..]r(?) / ]ꝑ q̄(?) / ]b[..] / ]ī ꝑ ante(?) /
            ][...]^a^ / ]sig̃m(?)
image-010:  ]n m[..] / ]aff'(?). / ]ue ꝯstā(?)
(Overlapping tile lines are listed once.)

SELECTED / UNREAD
- Selected: the two wider columns in full (they are the only places with
  several consecutive words per line), with special attention to underlined
  phrases and numeral references, since those are the most checkable:
    image-004 L14 / image-005 L3: underlined "ut xxx. q. iiii"
    image-004 L9: "c. i. ⁊ c. ..."
    image-008 L3: underlined "de clam. despon."
    image-002 L4, L10 and image-003 L7, image-004 L8, image-009 L8: other
    underlined phrases (only partly read).
- Connected sense I can vouch for only loosely. In the image-001 wide column the
  repeatedly legible word-shapes are "consang.." (five or more times), "uxor /
  uxoris / uxorem", "post mortem uxoris sue", "mortuam uxorem", "que duxit in
  ux..", "lineam desc..", "affin..". In the image-006 wide column: "sacerdos",
  "missam" (twice), "cum celebr.. missam", "ad altare", the sp-ōs- word (twice),
  "maxime", "consuet..". These are observations of vocabulary on the leaf, not
  an identification.
- Unread or effectively unread: image-002 L1-L3 and image-007 L1-L4 (dark and
  rubbed), image-003 L7, image-009 L9-L11, and both narrow columns as words.

LIMITATIONS
- Faint ink at low resolution; minims, c/t, s/f, and the many suspension strokes
  cannot be separated reliably. Treat every (?) as open and expect errors even
  in unmarked short words.
- Line counts are per tile from the first line visible in that tile; tiles
  overlap by two to three lines and I may be off by one line where a tile's
  top line is only half visible (image-003, image-004, image-005, image-008,
  image-009, image-010 all start mid-overlap).
- Which side is recto is not determinable. On image-001 the narrow column
  follows the wide one on the page; on image-006 the narrow column precedes the
  wide one (the two wide columns are back to back on the same part of the
  strip). The reading order of the four column-parts across the turn therefore
  depends on which side is recto, and I cannot settle that from the images.
- Needed for a firm reading: native-resolution (larger) crops of the two wide
  columns, ideally with raking or UV/IR light for the dark top third.
